The current Count Basie Orchestra is under the able leadership of trombonist Grover Mitchell. Grover first joined the Basie band in November of 1962 and led the trombone section for important years during the 60s and 70s. He has also performed with the great big bands of Duke Ellington and Lionel Hampton, and appears on many recordings with all of these ensembles. In Basie’s later years, Grover became an important companion and confidante for the Count.
As he himself puts it, “I grew into this job.”
Grover Mitchell was interviewed by Monk Rowe after a performance of the Basie Orchestra at the Sarasota Jazz Festival on April 13, 1996.

We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe, and we’re honored to have with us a man who has had a huge part in the two greatest jazz orchestras, welcome Grover Mitchell.
Oh, thank you. Thanks for having me.
Can you possibly describe to me that tempo that you did “Jumpin’ at the Woodside” to end that concert?

Oh, yeah. Yeah it’s a, you know that’s one of the success factors about this band is our ability to handle the extremely fast and the extremely slow, if you can remember “L’il Darling” and those things, how slow we played those things.
It’s almost a tradition with the Basie band to be able to generate excitement and swing but so soft and slow.
